HIP/Windows: select the GPU by its HIP ordinal, not the registry index

On a PC with an integrated GPU the engine ran the wrong device. setup.py
detects AMD cards through display-class enumeration (the registry), but
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES counts the devices the HIP runtime enumerates, and the
two orders differ: the iGPU takes ordinal 0 and pushes the discrete card to
1. So the 9070 XT was registry index 0 and HIP ordinal 1, and the config
pointed the engine at the iGPU, which the compiled-arch check then refused.

Confirmed on this PC: strata-device --list-devices reports
  device 0: AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics (gfx1036)   <- the iGPU
  device 1: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (gfx1201)      <- the card setup picked
and `setup.py --check` had chosen index 0 for the 9070 XT.

- device.hpp/device.cu: device_count(), so a caller can enumerate without
  tripping the arch check (which throws for a card the binary has no code
  for - exactly what a listing needs to show).
- device_main.cpp: --list-devices prints every device the runtime reports
  with its architecture and, where it differs, why this binary cannot run
  it. Without the arch check, since reporting those cards is the point.
- setup.py: hip_ordinal() resolves the card's HIP ordinal by matching the
  architecture on the line AFTER its "device N:" header. Matching on the
  name or on the text of the arch complaint would pick the iGPU: the
  complaint names this build's architectures, so "gfx1201 in line" matches
  the iGPU's error. The resolved ordinal goes into the config as
  "hip_ordinal", with a warning when it differs from the registry index.
- server.py: hip_visible() prefers the recorded ordinal, falling back to
  gpu_list() for a config written before this (right only without an iGPU).

Also fixes two defects found while building this on Windows:

- native_head.cpp: the destructor freed dev_owned_ and then dev_, but
  load() only ever sets one of them, so a device-resident table was freed
  twice. The stale dev_owned_ line came in with #247 and outlived the
  rewrite that removed its declaration.

HIP/Windows: docs, the requested _WIN32 gate, and a test for the mapped-alias finding

- absorb_hipblas_sticky is now gated on _WIN32 as well as __HIPCC__. The sticky
  hipErrorInvalidValue is a property of the Windows stack, and clearing it after
  every GEMM on Linux would hide a real error there.

- tests/hip/mapped_alias reports whether a hipHostGetDevicePointer alias is
  host-visible, which is the cause of tests/hip/handoff's gfx1201/Windows
  timeout. On Windows the alias IS the host pointer (both print as
  0x304000000), so a DeviceToDevice copy into it is a host address in a device
  pointer and publishes nothing. The test always exits 0 - a Windows host is
  expected to fail the host-visibility checks, and it is a diagnosis, not a gate.
  It skips the crashing copy rather than faulting the run.

- The same property is why native_head.cpp keeps the token embedding in device
  memory on Windows; docs/AMD_HIP.md now records it, and that handoff is left
  unfixed and named rather than papered over (the engine does not use that copy
  path on Windows - its arena arrives through cudaHostRegistered pinned memory).

- docs/AMD_HIP.md gains a Windows section (detection, ROCm + rocm-sdk init, VS
  Build Tools, the /FI force-include, hip_ordinal, the sticky error, the limits)
  and no longer scopes Windows HIP out. README lists the AMD cards on both
  platforms.

expert cache: hold back what is allocated after it, on one GPU as on two

The full model at IQ3_XXS could not start on a 16 GB card. The engine sized a
6,124-slot expert cache (9.92 GiB), printed "almost ready", and then died:

  strata serve: the penalty-history allocation failed

The penalty history is 0.1 MiB and there was under 128 KB spare. The layer split
already reserves for exactly this - stage_room() holds back kWindowMib and
kDrafterMib because the verify windows, the drafter and the head are allocated
after a stage's cache is sized. The single-GPU path reserved `vram_reserve_mib`
alone, and a profile-sized cache took the rest. The Coder survived only because
its cache is 0.33 GiB smaller; that was luck, not design.

- kPostCacheMib (192) beside kWindowMib/kDrafterMib, and the single-GPU sizing
  now holds it back too. 192 covers the measured 74.1 MiB of verify windows at
  n_embd 2560, the 0.1 MiB penalty history and the R4 hit-path scratch, which
  scales with n_embd. kDrafterMib is deliberately not re-added: mtp_bind is this
  run's own figure for those bytes.
- The profile-sizing pass re-read cudaMemGetInfo and capped against
  `vram_reserve_mib` alone, handing the slack straight back. It now keeps the
  same amount.
- The failure message names the cause and the fix instead of just reporting the
  fact: how big the buffer was, how much VRAM was actually free, and that
  --vram-reserve-mib is the lever.

Measured on an RX 9070 XT (gfx1201, 16 GB), ROCm 10.2.0, full model IQ3_XXS at
32K, at the DEFAULT reserve with no --vram-reserve-mib:

  before: 6,124 slots / 9.92 GiB, then "the penalty-history allocation failed"
  after:  6,009 slots / 9.73 GiB, 662 MiB VRAM free, serves at 27.7-35.6 tok/s

That is MORE cache than the --vram-reserve-mib 2048 workaround managed (5,303

bench: context x quant decode matrix, and the harness traps that produced it

Generation tok/s for the full model on an RX 9070 XT (gfx1201, 16 GB), int8 KV,
median of 3 x 160-token generations:

             32K    131K   262K
  IQ2_XS    27.5    24.0   23.2     7,546 / 6,396 / 5,043 cache slots
  IQ3_XXS   25.3    21.8   22.0     6,009 / 5,050 / 3,915

The interesting results:

- An 8x longer window costs ~15% of decode, not 8x. Context length costs VRAM, and
  the KV cache takes it out of the expert cache (0.43 -> 3.42 GB over 32K..262K),
  which costs ~1,100 cached experts. The model is expert-bound, not context-bound:
  only ~10 of 24,576 experts are used per token, so the hit rate sets the pace.
- IQ2_XS is FASTER than IQ3_XXS. The more precise quant stores bigger blobs, so
  fewer of them fit in the same VRAM (6,009 vs 7,546 slots at 32K) with more dequant
  work per token. On a 16 GB card, fitting more of the model beats storing it more
  precisely.

Three harness traps, each of which produced a wrong number first:

- Repeating one prompt measures the server's conversation cache, not generation.
  That reported an impossible 160 tok/s. Every trial now carries a random salt and
  is rejected if the server reports cached prompt tokens.
- Three trials is too few here. Per-trial spread is 19.3-26.4 tok/s, and the first
  requests after a reload run at ~8 tok/s while the path warms, so a 3-trial median
  put 262K above 131K - backwards, since 131K has 1,135 more slots. repeat_bench.py
  prints every trial; the writeup says which columns are within noise.
- The log parse assumed the free-VRAM number was the first field, so it raised
  ValueError on "strata" and a whole six-cell run reported success with no data.

mtp: the draft chain in one graph launch with a WHILE node (#16)

The chain tested each draft's probability on the host between one graph
and one stream synchronization per step. A conditional WHILE node now
makes that test on the device (mtp_chain_next), so a round is two graph
launches and one synchronization. Every step runs the same kernels on
the same values; the step record the host staged for step j is copied
into one fixed row by mtp_chain_stage. STRATA_OLD_MTP_CHAIN=1 keeps the
per-step graphs, which are also used when the driver refuses the
conditional node. mtp_chain_parity checks the chain against the host
loop.

verify: a commit the host need not wait for; flag B by a stream write (#16)

commit(n, err, wait = false) launches the commit graph and records an
event instead of synchronizing: the next window follows on the same
stream and the MTP round can wait for the event on the device.
sync_commit() waits for such a commit; STRATA_OLD_COMMIT_SYNC=1 restores
the synchronization. The default (wait = true) is unchanged.

In DMA mode, flag B is raised by cuStreamWriteValue32 queued behind the
copies instead of a host function (STRATA_OLD_DMA_FLAG=1 keeps the host
function; it is also the fallback). Once a raise is queued in a window,
the later raises of that window are queued too, so the flag only rises.

generate: speculative loops without the commit sync or a thread per adaptive round (#16)

Both decode loops (--serve and --spec) commit without waiting (the next
window follows on the verify stream, the MTP round waits for the commit
event) and wait once when the loop ends. The residency table goes up
asynchronously from a pinned copy on the refill stream (no window reads
it; the loop's end waits for it), and the adaptive tier's host work runs
on one persistent thread (round_sync.hpp). STRATA_OLD_COMMIT_SYNC=1,
STRATA_OLD_RES_UPLOAD=1 and STRATA_OLD_ADAPT_THREAD=1 restore each
previous behavior.

platform: concurrent Linux DirectFile reads through io_uring or a pread pool (#15)

A read no longer completes inside submit on Linux, so the 16 reads of a
token run in parallel, wake() works and --ple-inflight sizes the queue.
io_uring (raw syscalls, no liburing) is the default where the kernel
allows it; a pool of min(queue depth, 16) pread threads is the fallback.
STRATA_PLE_IO_BACKEND=uring|threads|sync picks one; sync is the previous
path, kept as the A/B arm.

ngram: submit reads outside the reader lock; split gather_batch in two (#15)

The reader's worker makes its submit calls without holding its mutex, so
issue and collect on the host thread never wait behind a read. PleTable
gains issue_batch/collect_batch (the same bytes as gather_batch), and the
io report names the read backend.

verify: read the PLE rows while the GPU runs layer 0 (#15)

The window graph no longer copies the PLE rows at its head: it waits on a
mapped flag just before layer 1 and copies them there. The host starts the
reads before the launch and collects them after serving layer 0's first
group, so the SSD reads overlap the embedding, layer 0 and the CPU experts
instead of delaying the launch. Same bytes, same kernels, same arithmetic;
STRATA_OLD_PLE_STAGING=1 restores the read-before-launch path.
ple_stage_parity checks the flag handshake on a replayed graph.

prefill: gdn_conv as a thread per (channel, token), the q/k norm in the same kernel (#37)

The 4-tap causal conv is a FIR: output t reads only inputs t-3..t (the history
below t = 0). A block now covers one head of 128 channels and 16 tokens, loads
the 19 inputs once, and applies the L2 norm of the 32 q/k heads before writing;
a small kernel then writes the new history. 80 x T/16 blocks instead of 80
threads walking 8192 tokens in series, and one pass over h instead of two.

Same operations in the same order as gdn_conv_kernel + gdn_l2_kernel (the SASS
of both has the same FMUL/FFMA chain and the same unfused square before the
warp sum), so the result is bitwise identical. STRATA_OLD_PREFILL_GDN_CONV=1
selects the previous kernels. prefill_kernels_parity compares both, bitwise.

pool: run_split cuts each phase into 3 x threads equal row ranges across all its experts (#27)

The per-expert parts gave 10 experts on 6 threads 20 tasks (4/4/3/3/3/3), and the
last wave ran on 2 threads of 6.  The flat cut is run_split_multi's; every row still
goes through the same row_dot, so the result is bitwise the same.
STRATA_OLD_RUN_SPLIT=1 keeps the per-expert parts for the A/B.

pool_test --synthetic runs the checks on random experts (a new ctest,
pool_test_synthetic) and adds run_split in both cuts and run_split_multi, bitwise
against serial.  pool_test --bench times run_split per token, both cuts, and on
Linux the flat cut again on an arena with transparent huge pages.

expert_source, s2_expert_grouped: guard the verify window's fixed tables (#11)

kind/distinct/first_of[128] in expert_pool_dispatch_multi hold MAXT x k entries:
a static_assert for MAXT x 10 <= 128 and a run-time refusal of any k that would
not fit, instead of writing past them.  The grouped GPU kernels keep at most

pinned: MADV_HUGEPAGE on the 4 KB fallback of the expert arena; report the share (#28)

Without a hugetlb pool the arena fell back to 4 KB pages, ~338 per expert and a TLB
miss on nearly each since the experts are drawn at random.  madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE)
before cudaHostRegister (which faults the arena in) asks for transparent huge
pages; the note then gives AnonHugePages against Rss from /proc/self/smaps.
STRATA_NO_THP=1 is the A/B arm.

iq_avx512: gathered grid lookups, vpermi2b sign lookups, an aligned copy of the activations (#30)

The i-quant rows were bound by their decode (~5 GB/s per core): 8 or 16 scalar grid
lookups inserted lane by lane and 8 scalar sign lookups per 64 values.  decode_g does
the grid lookups with one gather and the sign lookups with one vpermi2b over the
128-byte sign table held in two registers.  The tokens' Q8_K values are copied once
per call to 64-byte-aligned rows 3,648 bytes apart: in a block_q8_K every 64-value
load straddled two cache lines, and the pool's activations are exactly 4,096 bytes
apart, the same L1 set for every token.  Same bytes, same operations after the
decode: bitwise the previous kernel, which STRATA_OLD_IQ512=1 keeps for the A/B
(STRATA_IQ512_NOPACK=1: the gathers without the copy).

iq512_test (a ctest) checks the three builds bitwise on synthetic rows of every
format, 1..8 tokens, and the previous kernel against ggml's vec_dot; --bench times
them.

prefill: the dense projections through MMQ behind --prefill-dense-mmq (#39)

The native (GGUF) projections of the prompt path - GDN qkv/gate/out, QSA
q/k/v/o, the shared expert - were dequantized to FP16 and multiplied by cuBLAS
in FP16 with FP32 accumulation, half rate on GeForce. With --prefill-dense-mmq
(or STRATA_PREFILL_DENSE_MMQ=1) Gemm::native_mmq runs them through llama.cpp's
MMQ kernels, already built for the experts, in their plain dense mode (the launch
ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q makes: no row table, no bounds). The weights stay in their
blocks, the activations are rounded to q8_1 - from the FP32 rows where the path
keeps them (mixed, the GDN output), else from the FP16 ones widened - and the
products run on int8 tensor cores.

The q8_1 rows live in the dequantization scratch, in token slices when a
chunk's do not fit. A weight whose rows are not a multiple of 512 values (the
shared expert's down, K = 640) is copied there with a zeroed tail: MMQ's last
K tile reads past the matrix. IQ1_M (not covered by MMQ), beta != 0 or a build
without MMQ keep the FP16 path.

Off by default: q8_1 activations change the rounding, to be judged by
teacher-forced KL as the MMQ experts were. strata_mmq now also builds the
Q4_0, Q5_0, Q8_0 and Q3_K..Q6_K instances. gemm.hpp's header described a BF16
GEMM for the quantized weights; it is FP16.

tests: prefill_dense_mmq_parity, the dense MMQ path against cuBLAS and FP64 (#39)

A ctest on the GPU with synthetic weights quantized by ggml, for the 15 types
the dense path covers: every output finite, within 3% (relative RMS) of the
exact product - the q8_1 rounding of the activations, ~0.65% on these data -
and, for the D4-layout types, within 2e-3 of the product with the activations
rounded as MMQ's quantizer rounds them. Also: a second run bitwise identical,
the columns past N untouched (ldy > N), N not a multiple of 128, one token,
the FP16 activations widened, token slices against one pass, the K = 640
shape with NaN bytes planted after the weight (the padded copy must keep them
out), and the calls that must be declined (no context, IQ1_M, beta = 1, a
scratch too small).

s_gemv: the q8 split kernel reaches its barrier before a rowless warp returns (#2)

s_gemv_q8_split_kernel returned for o >= n_out before the codebook load and
__syncthreads(), so with n_out % 8 != 0 the last block's surplus warps left
before a barrier the others still waited at. Every shape in the pack is a
multiple of 8, so it was latent. The load and the barrier now come first, as
in s_gemv_q8k_kernel; the return stays warp-uniform. Same registers (48, no
spill), same arithmetic.

The Q8_0 launcher checked group_elems % 4 while a lane-iteration takes 16
elements under one scale; it now refuses anything but a multiple of 16, like
the Q8_K launcher (every group size the format defines is 16, 32 or 64).

s_gemv_q8k_parity runs both split kernels at n_out 1, 7, 9 and 61 against the
host reference, with a guard band past n_out that must stay untouched.

prefill: STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING times the dense projections apart and the QSA attention per chunk (#41)

Every native (GGUF) projection - GDN qkv/gate/out, QSA q/k/v/o, the shared
expert - is now its own phase, "dense proj" (what --prefill-dense-mmq
changes), taken out of gdn / qsa proj / router+shared. The marks also carry
their chunk: after the per-phase line, one line for the prompt and one per
chunk give the GPU time, "qsa attn" (the decode kernel, 32 queries per
launch), "qsa indexer+select" and "dense proj" with their shares. A chunk
attends to every position before it, so these lines show how the attention's
share grows with depth - the measurement #41 asks for before any new
attention kernel. Timing only: nothing is recorded without the variable.

prefill: the GDN recurrence on 4 blocks per value head, the output norm in a second pass (#38)

The 128 state columns of a value head evolve independently; only the RMS norm
of the output couples them. gdn_rec_split_kernel runs a (48 heads x 4 column
quarters) grid of 128 threads: a warp holds 8 columns x the same 4 row groups of
32 rows as before (lane = 4 * column + group), so kv and o are the old partial
sums, added in the old order through shuffles. q|k go through double-buffered
shared memory (one barrier per token instead of six) and the next token's q, k,
v, gate and beta are loaded while the current one runs. o * rsqrt(128) goes
through y; gdn_out_norm_kernel then applies the norm per (token, head) with the
old per-warp butterfly and the old order of the four warp sums.

Every operation is the old one in the old order (SASS checked: the fused
v - g * kv, the folded rsqrt(128), the unfused square, ss * 1/128 + eps), so y,
its FP16 bits and the state are bitwise identical; the default path takes it.
STRATA_OLD_PREFILL_GDN_REC=1 selects the previous kernel.

bf16: a NaN stays a quiet NaN in f32 -> bf16, as in ggml (#13)

The rounding add carried out of the mantissa for a NaN: 0x7FFFFFFF became
0x8000 (-0) and 0x7F800001 became 0x7F80 (+inf), so a NaN upstream was masked
instead of propagated. bf16_from_f32 (bf16_bits.hpp) and dequant_bf16.cu's own
f2bf now test the magnitude first and return (u >> 16) | 64, which is
ggml_compute_fp32_to_bf16. Every non-NaN input, infinities included, rounds
exactly as before.

bf16_bits_test (CPU, ctest) checks the header against ggml's function and
against the previous rule on all 2^32 f32 patterns; elementwise_parity checks
f32_to_bf16_bulk and a Q8_0 block with a NaN scale through dequant_bf16.

generate: --spec without a drafter verifies one token per window, not zeros (#10)

With --spec but neither --mtp nor --spec-oracle (a native pack requires --spec,
not --mtp) every window was padded to T with token 0: drafts rejected at once,
each a full token of verify work. The window is now the last token alone, and
the suffix lookup still widens it when it proposes a repeat (DraftPolicy picks
between T = 1 and the lookup window). A rejected draft never emits, so the
output is unchanged. STRATA_OLD_SPEC_FILL=1 restores the padded windows.

rope_parity: the native RoPE at positions 0 to 262144 against float64 (#3)

The production path (--native) rotates with native_rope, llama.cpp's f32 angle
under --use_fast_math (__powf, __sinf, __cosf); rope_parity only reached
position 31 and never ran it. A probe row per position (x = 1 on the first
half, 0 on the second) returns (cos, sin) of the device's angle, so the phase
error of all 32 pairs is read back directly and printed per position, with the
error of rotated random rows and the in-place (x == out) bits.

The assertion is an error model, not a measurement: the worst pair loses at
most ~4.3e-7 * pos radians (theta_scale^p in f32, lg2/ex2 approximations, the
f32 product, and the f32 turn fraction before the hardware sine); 1e-4 + 1e-6 *
pos is allowed, 2.3x that and ~4x under the 1 rad of an off-by-one position.

pool: the native down activations one line more than 1 KB apart; iq512_test --bench times ggml's single-token dot (#30)

hq[t] and hq[t + 4] were exactly 4 KB apart, the same L1 set.  The bench prints
ggml-cpu's vec_dot beside the one-token row, which is what native_gu_rows runs for
an expert routed a single token.

expert: software prefetch of the scale and code streams; opt-in integer correction of the down rows (#29)

(a) STRATA_CPU_PREFETCH=<bytes> prefetches the scale stream, STRATA_CPU_PREFETCH_CODES=
<bytes> the code stream, that far ahead of the row being computed, in every Q2_0
row loop (single-token, multi-token, row ranges).  No result changes.

(b) STRATA_CPU_INT_CORR=1: the 512-bit down rows start vpdpbusd from -sum(xhat) of
each chunk (a seed act_quant_q8_1 writes into ActQ), so the Q2_0 code offset is
removed exactly in integer and the float correction - its accumulator, an FMA per
eight blocks and a second reduction - is gone; also for the GGUF-layout Q2_0 down
rows of the native packs.  It changes the last bits, so it is opt-in; single- and
multi-token kernels still agree bitwise with each other in either mode.

expert_multi_test checks both modes, with and without prefetch, and the integer
correction against the default and the scalar oracle; --bench times the arms.
pool_test --bench adds the prefetch arms and --workers N.

sampler: top_k by a lexicographic threshold, FP64 tail on one warp (#20)

sampler_kernel excluded the logits already kept by sweeping the kept list for
every logit of every round: O(k^2 x n_vocab) shared-memory compares per row
(47 M at top_k 20, 500 M at 64) on one SM.  Round i now takes the logits
strictly after round i-1's pick in the selection order (value descending, id
ascending): exactly the set the sweep left, so the list and its order are
unchanged.  The top_p / min_p / temperature / draw tail ran in double on all
1,024 threads; one warp now shares the exps and the quotients and lane 0 runs
the ordered sums and scans, with the same arithmetic.

The previous kernel stays selectable with STRATA_OLD_SAMPLER=1.

sampler: split the sampled top_k over the whole GPU (#20)

The sampled path kept a row on one SM and walked its 248,320 logits k times.
Stage 1 now cuts each row into 4,096-logit blocks (61 per row): each warp holds
1,024 penalised logits in registers and keeps their top_k with the same
threshold rounds, and the block merges its four warp lists.  Stage 2, one warp
per row, merges the block lists and runs the one-warp tail.  The first k of a
union are within the first k of each part and a merge of ordered lists is
ordered, so the list, its order and the pick are unchanged.

Default for vocabularies up to 262,144; the one-block kernel remains the
fallback (stream capture, wider vocabulary, no scratch) and is selectable with
STRATA_SAMPLER_ONE_BLOCK=1.  The block lists live in a per-stream scratch
buffer grown on demand.

iq_kernels: decode each IQ weight part once for every column and entry (#18)

iq_mmvq, native_gu_kernel and native_down_kernel called the format's dot once
per column (or group entry), re-reading the weight words and redoing the grid
lookups and sign unpacking each time. Each dot is now split into load (weight
side) and apply (activation side, same integer chain and float expression), as
native_mmvq.cu's multi-column traits are: the dense kernel takes 1, 2, 4 or 8
columns per pass (8 at a time past 8), the grouped ones 4 entries per pass
(~48 registers, a split verify window in one pass).

Every column keeps the same calls, lane stride, summation order and warp_sum,
so results are bitwise equal to the old kernels, which STRATA_OLD_IQ_MMVQ=1 (or
iq_set_old_kernels) keeps for A/B timing. iq_multi_parity (ctest, GPU,
synthetic) checks old vs new bitwise for every format, ncols 1..8 and 11,
groups of 0..11 entries; --bench times both.

gdn_fused_parity: the --native GDN kernels over 256 steps, and the three softplus forms (#8, #5)

fused_gdn_step_norm, fused_gdn_ab, fused_gdn_conv_l2 (the --native default)
and the native_gdn_* chain (--no-fused-gdn) had no test, and gdn_parity only
ever takes one step. The new test carries the legacy, native and fused step
kernels through the same 256 inputs against one float64 state, in a mixed and
a long-memory gate regime, and prints the drift at steps 1, 16, 64 and 256
(tolerance 5e-6 + 2e-7 * step: a host model of the fused order drifts ~2e-7,
and 1.3e-5 with every decay biased 2 ulp the same way). It also checks
fused_gdn_ab against float64 over every softplus regime, fused_gdn_conv_l2,
and the native conv+SiLU, L2 norm, beta and output norm.

Softplus (#5): the native gate is ggml-cuda's op_softplus verbatim
(logf(1 + expf(v)), threshold 20, fast-math), so it reproduces llama.cpp and
stays as it is; the comment says so. It is exactly 0 below v ~ -17, where the
fused log1pf(__expf(v)) and the legacy log1pf(expf(v)) are not. The test
asserts the native form against llama.cpp's expression, the fused one against
float64, and prints the gap per range of v.

sampler_parity: the top_k list under ties, tied draws, every sampled path (#20)

Fixture 16 reads the kept list position by position: every row holds a +inf
logit, so the tail's arithmetic is NaN and the chain returns sel_ids[k - 1];
top_k 1..64 then pins the list's set and order.  The rows put hundreds of
logits on the same values across every split block, warp and lane, tie -0
with +0, mix in -inf and NaN, run out of candidates (the id-0 sentinel) and
land penalised tokens exactly on other tokens' values; vocabularies 248,320,
100,003, 262,144, 262,145 (the one-block fallback) and 1,000.  Fixture 17
draws through the whole chain on half-step logits with and without penalties,
17 rows, on the legacy stream and on a created one.  Both compare with a mirror
of the kernel's own semantics (-inf and NaN never kept, id 0 when nothing is
left).

ctest runs the binary once per path: sampler_parity (split),
sampler_parity_one_block and sampler_parity_old.  --bench times the sampled
path the environment selects at the engine's vocabulary.

fused_gr_parity: the fused hyper-connection read against float64, and T tokens bitwise one (#8)

fused_gr_read runs twice per layer per token with --native and
fused_gr_read_multi in every verify window and MTP draft; neither had a test.
The single read is checked against a float64 transcription of fused_gr.hpp's
contract (rs, lo, inject, mixed, and R updated in place), with and without the
folded write and the injection rows. The multi read is asserted BITWISE equal
to the single read of each token for T = 1..8 with a different R, pending
write and injection per token, outputs poisoned beforehand - the header
promises it and the verify window's exactness depends on it.

prefill: the GR chain keeps the row scales, not the FP32 xn; the write carries the next half's norm (#43)

gr_norm wrote xn in FP32 and BF16, gr_mix read the FP32 xn back, and the next
gr_norm read R again right after gr_write had written it. Now:
- gr_norm_scale writes the BF16 image and the scale of each (token, stream)
  row; gr_mix_scale recomputes xn = (R * rs) * w, the product gr_norm stored;
- gr_write_norm updates a row in registers, writes it, and normalizes it with
  the next half's weight, with gr_norm's thread-to-element map (same sum of
  squares). The prompt path uses it when nothing else writes R in between:
  always within a layer, and across layers unless the control vector covers
  the layer or the next layer is layer 1 with the PLE block.
m.xn shrinks to the row scales (T*4 floats instead of T*10240: 335 MB less at
T = 8192, in carve and bytes_needed alike).

Bitwise identical by construction (same SASS arithmetic: the FFMA sum of
squares, the FMUL pair of xn, the FFMA of the write). STRATA_OLD_PREFILL_GR=1
restores gr_norm / gr_mix / gr_write and the FP32 xn buffer.

router_top10_parity: the native router through the same four distributions (#8)

native_router_top10 (the pinned topk-moe contract, fast-math, --native) had no
test. It now runs the random, all-equal, 12-way tie and dominant-expert logits
one token per launch against the same host reference: ids exact, ties to the
lower index included, weights within 1e-5 relative.

bf16_gemv_parity: the native MMVF bitwise against a host emulation of its order (#8)

bf16_gemv_fp32_mmvf (llama.cpp's MMVF order, the F32-activation contract of
--native) had no test. Its order is fully specified - thread t of a block of B
takes pairs t, t + B, ... with two ordered fmaf, xor-butterfly per warp, then
over the warp sums - so the host emulates it exactly (B from a transcription
of mmvf_block_size). Seven shapes cover block sizes 32, 128, 160 and 256:
every row must match the emulation bit for bit and float64 within 1e-5.

quantize_act_parity: the scaled Q8_0 quantizer bit for bit against act_quant_q8_1 (#8)

quantize_q8_0_scaled exists so that a GPU hit and a CPU miss of the same
expert quantize the activation identically, and nothing checked it. The test
now links strata_kernels_cpu and compares against the real act_quant_q8_1 (its
AVX2 form on a CPU without AVX-512): int8 codes and fp32 scales bit-identical,
the block's fp16 d the scale rounded, over random, tiny, large, zero-chunk and
exact-tie activations. The tie fixture is asserted able to tell half-away from
half-even first.

kv_q4_parity: the gathered values are asserted, not only printed (#8)

Test 4 printed the reconstruction error and reported OK whatever it was. Each
gathered FP16 value must now equal the host's dequantization of the host's
own Q4_0 block (f16((q - 8) * d16), low nibble first), and lie within Q4_0's
bound of the raw value: 1.01 |d16| + |x| / 1024 (half a step, a full step
where x/d >= 7.5 clamps to code 15, plus the fp16 rounding of d and of the
output).

prefill: FP16 images can saturate at +-65504 instead of overflowing to inf (#6), opt-in

hf() fed every FP16 image of the prompt path with __float2half_rn: a finite
value past 65520 became +-inf (the shared expert's SwiGLU products, y_h,

kernels: multi-column BF16 MMVF and a batched native router (#19)

(native_swiglu_quantize_q8_1, sharing the quantizer's body; the SwiGLU is the

kernels: S2 expert kernels without bank conflicts or per-row hx, wide loads (#17)

The grouped kernels (verify window, MTP layer) staged each entry's activations as
xs_q[k][c * 8 + j], an 8-way bank conflict on every read, and recomputed the chunk
sum hx with eight dp4a for every row. The per-hit kernels (token graph) read each
chunk with 44 byte loads.

New kernels, default on, bitwise identical to the previous ones:
- activations regrouped once per chunk so the codes expand with shift+mask
  (seven operations per 16 elements) and hx is summed once per chunk;
- grouped: word-major shared layout xs_w[j][k * NC + c] plus (dx, hx) pairs,
  conflict-free on both the staging writes and the reads, two rows per warp;
- per hit: nine aligned word loads per activation chunk, uint2 code loads,
  16-bit scale loads, one warp per (gate, up) pair or pair of down rows.

s, hx and the float expression dw * dx * (float) (s - hx) are unchanged, so every
output matches the previous kernels bit for bit. STRATA_OLD_GROUPED=1 (or
moe_grouped_select_old(1)) selects the previous kernels for A/B, and so does any
activation row or blob arena the wide loads cannot take.

tests: s2_expert_grouped_parity, previous vs new expert kernels bitwise (#17)

iq_multi_parity checks the fast quantizer against native_quantize_q8_1

prefill: the token path's router for the prompt, opt-in; router rows with non-finite logits in debug (#7)

The prompt router (route_kernel) uses the precise expf; the token path's
native router is compiled with --use_fast_math, and without --native-router
the token path uses router_top10 (double). Near a tie the prompt and the

masks a NaN probability as -FLT_MAX, and a row of NaN takes experts 0-9

A group's n * NH query heads are rows of one pitch in qfull_ and qcur_, pos_
holds a position per row, and the norm, rotation, FWHT and output gate kernels
(native and legacy) are per row or per element: each is now called once per

window_batch_parity checks every kernel involved, batched against per token.

columns: every column of a multi-column call must equal a one-column call on

prefill: the chunk's indexer keys appended in two launches (#40)

The QSA layers of a prompt chunk appended their indexer keys one launch
per cell: 8192 x 12 launches per chunk, each with its host-side checks.
native_qsa_indexer_append_chunk leaves the buffers exactly as that loop
did: one block per event of the chunk (the spare key at cell 0, each
completed block) with the per-cell kernel's arithmetic statement for
statement (same PTX sequence), reading only the tail as the chunk found
it and the chunk's own keys; a second launch writes the spare row after
the last completed block, block_pos and the tail. The per-cell kernel is
unchanged (decode and the verify window still use it).

STRATA_OLD_IDX_APPEND=1 keeps the per-cell loop. qsa_indexer_chunk_parity
checks every byte of both buffer sets after every chunk (alignments, short
and 8192-cell chunks, the multimodal table, cells past the capacity).

prefill: routed pairs grouped by expert on the device, experts walked by group (#36)

Every MoE layer of a prompt chunk copied the T x 10 routed ids to the
host, synchronized the stream, sorted them there and uploaded two row
tables; then each expert cost ~6 API calls (a wait, a gather launch, a
release event, and on the copy stream a wait, a copy and an event).

- moe_group: the same counting sort on the GPU (per-chunk counts, a scan,
  each chunk's pairs placed in pair order by one warp with match_any), so
  slot/src are the host sort's tables entry for entry. Only the 512 counts
  come back, into pinned memory, and the host waits for them on an event
  while the shared expert runs. The group bounds go up from pinned memory.
- The grouped walk (stream_all chunks, every layer through MMQ): a group of
  experts waits once for the copies up to its last entry, is gathered in
  one launch (gather_native_batch / gather_strata_q2_batch, byte for byte
  the per-expert gathers) and gives its ring slots back with one event.
  Up to 16 consecutive experts of a layer that lie back to back in pinned
  RAM come in with one 2D copy (STRATA_PREFILL_COALESCE=0: one per expert).
  The MMQ products are launched exactly as before (same groups, same
  max_rows, same bounds), so the layer's output is bitwise unchanged.
- run() now also synchronizes the copy stream before returning: a streamed
  expert the routing did not pick is never waited for, and its copy lands
  in the borrowed slots that the caller refills.

STRATA_OLD_MOE_GROUP=1 restores the host sort and the per-expert walk.
moe_group_parity checks the tables against the host sort and the batched
gathers against the per-expert ones.

spec: the suffix drafter resets lazily and extends a continued history (#46)

Every serve request reset the drafter (a 16 MB table at 128K of context,
32 MB at 262K, rewritten) and hashed its whole prompt again. A slot now
carries the epoch it was written in and a slot of an older epoch reads as
empty, so reset() is O(1) (the table is cleared for real only when the
32-bit counter wraps); the slot stays 32 bytes. sync(tokens) appends only
the new tokens when the history is a prefix of them - a request that
continues the conversation - and resets otherwise. The index depends only
on the tokens appended since the last reset, so proposals are those of a
drafter rebuilt from scratch; suffix_drafter_test checks that against
fresh drafters (extended, rebuilt, after 1000 resets, and a small table
refilled in every epoch, which fails if stale slots stay occupied).

STRATA_OLD_SFX_RESET=1 rebuilds the history from the whole prompt.

qsa: mask cells whose page did not resolve; refuse a clock sweep over fewer slots than the resolve block (#12)

When KV streaming cannot place a block (ctl[3]), its page table entry stays -1 and
qsa_decode_attn computed a row index before the start of the pool. Such a cell now
gets row -1: score -FLT_MAX, weight 0, and its V row is never read. A chunk with no
resolvable cell reports m = -FLT_MAX and l = 0, which the merge already skips. With
every page resolved the added conditions are always true and the float arithmetic is
the same instruction sequence as before (compared on the PTX).

kv_stream_resolve refuses n_slots < 1024: one sweep step looks at RT consecutive
slots modulo n_slots, so with fewer slots two threads could take the same one. The
engine never streams with fewer than 5,120 slots; this is a guard.

serve: conversation checkpoints through a pool of pinned buffers (#45)

A checkpoint synchronized the device, then copied its ~118 MB of running
state (GDN recurrences and conv histories, PLE history, indexer tails)
with a synchronous cudaMemcpy per piece into freshly allocated pageable
vectors, whose pages the copy itself faulted in - at every turn boundary
and every 16384 prompt tokens. Each checkpoint now takes one buffer of a
pool of pinned buffers, handed back when the checkpoint is dropped (at
most --prompt-cache + 1 of them), and the pieces are queued on the pool's
stream with one wait; a restore goes back the same way. Pageable buffers
when no more RAM can be pinned. The bytes are the same.

STRATA_OLD_CKPT=1 keeps the pageable vectors and synchronous copies.

generate: the profile fill queued on one stream, the first and last slots verified (#48)

The startup fill of the VRAM tier made one blocking copy per slot (4,105
on a 12 GB card, ~16,000 on a 32 GB one), leaving the copy engine idle
between them. The fills are now queued on one stream and waited for once;
the slots hold the same bytes. With the fills asynchronous, the read-back
check covers the last slot filled as well as the first (1.38 MB each).
Only the first slot was ever read back, not every slot as #48 describes,
so the check itself was not the startup cost. The fill time is printed.

STRATA_OLD_PROFILE_FILL=1 keeps the blocking copies.

generate: opt-in asynchronous refill of the slots lent to the prompt path (#42)

After a batched prompt, the expert-cache slots lent to the prompt path
were refilled one blocking copy at a time before the first window (~180
ms when serving, several GB from the command line), outside the prompt's
reported rate. With STRATA_ASYNC_REFILL=1 the copies are queued on the
refill stream and the slots re-admitted through the adaptive tier's
`pending` list once they have landed (checked before every window, the
prompt's windows included); until then the CPU computes those experts.
A later lend waits for them first. The command line does the same when a
native pack's speculative loop follows the prompt.

Opt-in: the experts computed on the CPU instead of the GPU meanwhile
round differently, and when the copies land depends on timing.

qsa_select: block top-k with coalesced histogram passes and parallel scans (#22)

block_topk2_kernel (512 threads, one block per query) replaces block_topk_kernel
by default and selects exactly the same cells:
- the four 8-bit histogram passes read 32 consecutive blocks per warp, four loads
  ahead, into one histogram per warp; the lanes of a warp that fall in the same bin
  add once (__match_any_sync), with the exact cell weight of each block;
- the digit comes from a block-wide scan of the 256 bins (thread t holds digit
  255 - t), which evaluates the serial walk's rule at every digit at once, instead
  of up to 256 steps on thread 0 per pass;
- counting and emission give each warp a contiguous range of blocks, walked 32
  blocks at a time, and place each lane's cells with warp scans; the equal-key
  budget is spent in ascending cell order as before. The two 256-step serial
  prefixes on thread 0 are gone.
Every count is an integer sum, so the threshold, the budget and the emitted cells
are the previous kernel's. STRATA_OLD_TOPK=1 keeps the previous kernel (read once,
before capture); qsa_block_topk_set_old is the same switch for tests.

qsa_decode_attn: V rows prefetched with cp.async under QK and the softmax, K rows preloaded (#23)

attn_chunk_pf_kernel replaces attn_chunk_kernel by default. As soon as the page
table has resolved the chunk's rows, their V values start as cp.async copies into
shared memory (16-byte pieces: 32 KB per 64-cell chunk in fp16, 16 KB in int8 plus
the scales, 9 KB in q4_0); each warp loads its 8 K rows into registers before its
first dot product; the copies are waited for only before the value loop, which
reads shared memory. The previous kernel had one load in flight per warp in the
score loop and 64 serial 2-byte reads per thread in the value loop.

The arithmetic is the previous kernel's expression for expression (same load8, dot,
warp trees, fmaf chain over ascending cells, V decoded from the same bits), so the
partials are bitwise the same; the PTX shows the same mul + 7 fma.rn per dot.

aligned falls back to it.

STRATA_QSA_CHUNK=32 (opt-in) runs the prefetching kernel over 32-cell chunks: ~130
blocks instead of 66 on a 170-SM part, but a different split of the softmax, hence
a different rounding. The scratch size follows the variant, read once at start;
qsa_decode_attn_set_variant is the switch for tests.

q4_0 80 / 25.1 KB with an 8-byte spill; chunk 32: 48-62 registers, no spill.

qsa_decode_attn: the output gate folded into the merge, opt-in (STRATA_QSA_MERGE_GATE=1) (#23)

With QsaAttnGate set, attn_merge_gate_kernel applies the layer's gate to the value
it merges and writes the gated output as well: one launch less per QSA layer in the
decode layer (layer.cpp) and in the verify window (verify.cpp). Not with q4_0 KV,
whose output is rotated back between the attention and the gate.

- kQsaGateF64 is qsa_gate_apply_f32's source, in a TU built with the same flags;
  the PTX has the same fp64 operation sequence.
- kQsaGateNativeF32 is native_qsa_gate_apply, whose TU is fast-math: the
  instructions it emits (mul by -log2(e), ex2.approx, add, rcp.approx, mul, all

The merge body moved into merge_one, shared by both merge kernels (same float
operations as before). Opt-in until qsa_decode_attn_parity has confirmed on the

Tokenizer: cache the ids of pre-tokenizer pieces; resume points and PromptEncoder for incremental prompts (#32)

BPE is quadratic in a piece's length and pieces repeat, so the ids of pieces up to 64 characters are
kept in an LRU cache.  encode_marked() also returns where the encoding can resume after each special
token, and PromptEncoder re-encodes only what follows the last special-token boundary a prompt shares
with a recent one (with a look-ahead margin of max_special_len - 1, so a longer literal cannot start
before the cut): the ids are those of a full encode by construction.  token_bytes() gives a token's
raw bytes for the streaming detokenizer (#31).

conversations through PromptEncoder, and literal sets built to break a cut without the margin.

Server: stream the detokenizer and encode prompts incrementally (#31, #32)

Detokenizer: each token's bytes go through an incremental UTF-8 decoder instead of re-decoding
the whole answer per token (4.9 ms per token at 16K tokens measured here, now ~1 us).  The deltas
are the old ones, one for one: output is held while it ends in an incomplete character or a
U+FFFD, as the re-decode did.  STRATA_OLD_DETOK=1 keeps the re-decode.

Prompts go through PromptEncoder: only the text after the last special token shared with a recent
prompt is encoded again (a 101K-token conversation: 482 ms before, 3.7 ms for the next turn here).
STRATA_OLD_PROMPT_ENCODE=1 encodes every prompt in full; STRATA_CHECK_PROMPT_IDS=1 does both and
compares on every request.

Tests: the old and new detokenizers on random byte streams (invalid, cut and U+FFFD bytes) and on
the qwen35 vocabulary; six turns over HTTP give the ids of a full encode.

Server: find an image in the cache by its raw bytes, link one image's embeddings (#35)

The cache key was the hash of the NORMALIZED image, so Pillow decoded and re-encoded a WebP or TIFF
to PNG every turn it stayed in the conversation.  The key is now the hash of the bytes as sent, and
normalization runs only on a miss (the same bytes always give the same PNG, so the embeddings are
unchanged).  Hits refresh the entry's place, so eviction is least recently used.

A request with one image hard-links its cached embeddings instead of copying them (~10 MB), and the
request's file is made while the FIFO is held, so no other encode can evict what it is made of.

Tests: a fake encoder process; the second encode of a WebP never reaches normalize or the encoder; a
one-image request's file is the cached one and survives the request's cleanup; two images are
concatenated in order.

chat.py sends each answer's reasoning back; chat.py and the web app say when a new thinking level re-reads the chat (#34, #33)

The template renders past answers with their reasoning; chat.py kept only the content, so
every turn's prompt left the engine's live sequence right after <think> and the previous answer was
read again.  It now returns reasoning_content (--drop-thinking: the answers alone, as before).

The thinking level is written at the start of the prompt, so changing it mid-conversation makes the
engine read everything again: /think says so, and so do the web app's Sampling drawer (a hint under

warp per row): 12 SMs of a 170-SM RTX 5090, and each lane walked its 10
chunks of the 2560-wide row with a DRAM round trip every few chunks.

Each row now has its own block of 128 threads (96 blocks).  All of them
load the row into shared memory at once (at most 4 chunks each, every load
in flight together; x too for the single token), then:
  * fused_gdn_ab: warp 0 runs the warp-per-row chain unchanged;
  * gdn_ab_multi: warp w runs tokens w and w + 4, each (lane, token) chain

kernels: GDN step on a cluster of 4 blocks per head, bitwise (#26)

value head: 48 SMs carry the 6.3 MB of recurrent state traffic, whatever
the GPU.  On sm_90 and newer a head's 128 columns are now split over a
thread block cluster of 4 blocks (32 columns x 4 row groups, 192 blocks).

A column's arithmetic is the old kernel's line for line.  The head-wide RMS
norm is the only coupling: warp 0 of each block holds 32 consecutive columns
with the same lane per column as the old warp, so its butterfly is the same,
and it pushes its sum into every block of the cluster (distributed shared
memory); after a cluster barrier ss adds the same four warp sums in the
same order.  The multi-token kernel defers the norm of every output token
past the token loop (one cluster barrier per launch) and keeps the kv and o
partials in separate arrays: 4 block barriers per token instead of 6.

The launcher uses the cluster kernels only when the device supports
clusters, the kernel was compiled for sm_90+ (an older build is an empty
stub) and the cluster configuration is launchable; the checks run once,
with the capture mode relaxed.  STRATA_OLD_GDN_STEP=1 restores the
block-per-head kernels.

fix(engine): clear stale error/cancellation state between requests and before prompt prefill

When a request is cancelled during prompt reading (e.g. client disconnect

pool: enumerate the cpuset the kernel actually gave us

On this machine sched_getaffinity's kernel mask spans every POSSIBLE
cpu - 24,024 bits inside a container on a big host - while cpu_set_t
holds 1,024.  glibc's wrapper writes the kernel-sized mask past the
fixed struct, the enumeration then read what the overflow had left on
the stack, and the pool spawned 24,023 unpinned spin-wait workers: the
PC stopped being usable while Strata ran.  Ask the kernel for a mask
sized to hardware_concurrency (CPU_ALLOC), enumerate only that, and
clamp the default worker count to the same number.  Measured on the
broken machine: 24,023 workers before, 23 after.

serve: the conversation cache - continue from the consumed state

The serve loop zeroed the whole session and re-processed the full
prompt for EVERY request, which is why an ongoing chat paid full
time-to-first-token on each turn.  The loop now keeps the exact token
sequence the session state has consumed (the prompt plus every
generated token the verify windows fed back) and, when a following
request strictly extends it, skips the zeroing and re-prefill and
processes only the new tail.  Any divergence - a shorter prompt, a
different prefix, a new conversation - resets the state and takes the
full path, which keeps the semantics exact.

Verified on the IQ3_XXS artifact: the reuse path and a from-scratch
reprocessing of the same extended prompt produce identical tokens, and
the shipped IQ3 decode still returns its known-good continuation.

serve: per-request temperature sampling for the verify window's head

Temperature was ignored because the verify window's head sampling was
pinned to greedy INSIDE the captured CUDA graph (verify.cpp hardcoded
sp.greedy = true), and the GEN protocol carried no sampling keys.

- the sampling moves OUT of the captured graph: the graph computes the
  head logits, and run() applies sample_tokens host-side after the
  replay, with that request's own parameters and a fresh Philox counter
  per window (a captured sampler would replay the same draws forever)
- the GEN protocol accepts optional key=value pairs before the ids:
  temperature=, top_p=, top_k=, seed=; absent keys stay greedy, exactly
  as before
- server.py forwards the request's temperature/top_p/top_k/seed
- emitted tokens are always the TARGET's own samples (the drafts only
  fill the verified window), so the output distribution is the target's
  regardless of what the drafts propose

sampled requests with the same seed replay identically.

verify: a persistent per-request draw counter; sampled requests default top_k=20

The sampled path requires top_k in 1..64 (the selection loop is
O(k*n_vocab) by design); with the engine-default top_k=0 it returned
without writing the token, leaking stale buffer contents as output.
Sampled requests now default to the sampler's own top_k=20.

The Philox draw counter also must persist across a request's verify
windows - it was read from a run-local variable that reset every
window, so every window redrew the same numbers (identical sampled

perf: sample the verify window's head with a block per token

The sampled chain ran in ONE thread per token (64-thread launch): top_k
alone was k sequential full-vocabulary scans with an inner sweep over the
taken list, and a verify window measured ~1.6 s in the sampler - sampled
requests decoded at 1.5 tok/s against 54 greedy.

The selection is k argmax rounds, so it parallelises exactly like the
greedy kernel: one block per token, the rounds back to back inside it,
each a two-level (warp, then block) reduction.  Ties resolve to the
lowest index (the serial scan's strict '>'), so the kept sequence - set
and order - is unchanged, and the top_p cut, temperature and Philox draw
read that order as before.  sampler_parity passes; a 248,320-vocab

pool: one worker per physical core on Linux, like the Windows path

The Linux branch of physical_cores() enumerated every logical cpu in the
affinity mask, so on an SMT machine the default pool put two AVX2
workers on each core (this box: 23 workers + the host over 12).  The
Windows branch has always grouped by core; the paper's six-core machine
ran six workers.  The siblings contend for the core's SIMD ports and
each finishes slower than the pair's half, so more workers was slower.

The kernel publishes the groups in sysfs thread_siblings_list; keep the
first member of each, in mask order, and fall back to the logical
enumeration when sysfs is missing.  Measured on the 5900X / IQ3_XXS
decode workload (greedy, 256 tokens, pinned expert tier): 23 logical
workers 53.4 tok/s median vs one-per-core 57.0-58.4 across three runs,
about +8-9%; prompt processing unchanged (471 tok/s either way).

serve: stay quiet when a client hangs up mid-response

A probe that closes the connection before reading the reply (or resets
it) makes the response write fail with EPIPE, and socketserver's
default handle_error printed the full traceback for every occurrence -
the console read like a crash even though the request thread just
ended and the server kept serving.  BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError
and TimeoutError are the client's timing; anything else still gets the
traceback.  Verified with early-close probes against a 404 path and
hard-RST clients: no output, ordinary requests unaffected.

serve: a client's Stop now stops the engine (`STOP` on the engine stdin)

Stop never reached the engine: the client aborts the HTTP request, the
server set its cancel event - which only stopped TOKENS FROM BEING
FORWARDED - and kept draining engine stdout while the engine decoded
the whole max_tokens in the background at full power.  Two gaps made it
worse: the engine protocol had no cancel at all, and the server noticed
a disconnect only when a write failed, which on a half-closed socket
took a full send buffer of SSE data (~470 tokens measured) to surface.

Engine side: while a request runs, a watcher thread owns stdin - a
`STOP` line raises a flag the verify loop checks between windows and
the prompt path checks at chunk boundaries, the committed tokens stay
in the history cache, and the request answers `DONE ... stop`; a
pipelined next request is handed back to the main loop instead of being
eaten; `QUIT` and end of stdin stop the current request too.  Measured:
stop during decode lands within one window (7 tokens / 191 ms of decode
past the abort), stop during prefill returns DONE at the chunk boundary
and a follow-up prompt resumes from the processed prefix, and a full
un-stopped run is token-identical to before.

Server side: detect the hangup with a non-blocking MSG_PEEK before each
streamed event instead of waiting for EPIPE, send `STOP` once, and
drain to DONE.  Anthropic and OpenAI streaming paths both covered;
non-stream requests are unchanged.

parity: run native_expert_parity on AVX2-only boxes too

guard checked only the quant type, so on a CPU without AVX-512 the
harness died with SIGILL before printing anything - exactly the boxes
that need it most, since the engine runs its AVX2 ggml path there.

(act_quant_any, q2_rows_any) and gate the iq512 section on

distance from float truth, which says the --expert-cache token
divergence is the two activation formats (GPU q8_1 vs the CPU's ggml
vec_dot_type) disagreeing by their own rounding, not a fault on either
side.  0 failures.

generate: residual control-vector projection from GGUFs

--control-vector-scaled FILE[:SCALE] (repeatable) loads a control-vector
GGUF - the abliterate format: direction.<L> tensors, one n_embd-wide
F32/F16/BF16 vector per layer - normalizes each direction and projects
the scaled component along it out of every hyper-connection residual
stream after that layer's FFN write.  --cvec-mode project and
--cvec-dir per-layer name the operation and its layout (the only
supported values); --control-vector-layer-range FIRST LAST restricts
which layers load directions, llama.cpp's flag, inclusive on both ends:
directions outside are never parsed nor uploaded, and a reversed range
is refused at argument validation.

The plan is static for the process (vectors uploaded once), so the
projections are ordinary nodes of the captured layer graphs.  The
projection runs in prefill, token decode and the verify window, always
right after the half's write it projects; fused GR is disabled for cvec
runs so the projection sees the completed layer residual.  A run
without the flags never touches the stream: an unloaded plan returns
before touching anything, so captured graphs and output are unchanged.

serve: sampling defaults from the run config

The run config's optional `sampling` block (temperature, top_p, top_k,
seed) sets defaults for the fields a request leaves out, so a client
that sends no sampling keys gets configured sampling instead of greedy.
The request's own fields always win: an explicit temperature=0 still
means greedy, and a field set to null falls back to the default.

Keys the sampled path does not implement yet (min_p, presence_penalty,
repetition_penalty, frequency_penalty) are named at startup and ignored
rather than silently dropped; unknown keys are reported the same way.
An invalid value (top_k outside 1..64, a non-positive seed, a negative
temperature) refuses to start the server - a typo'd config should not
quietly change sampling.

Verified with a spy engine through Service.run: defaults apply when the
request omits the fields, the request's own values win, a null field
falls back to the default, and a server without the block forwards the
request unchanged; the config validator rejects out-of-range values and
warns on the not-yet-implemented keys.

generate: min_p and the penalties ride the GEN line

The sampled chain's last two gaps close: `min_p` and the llama.cpp
penalty set (repeat/freq/present over a history window) are live end
to end - GEN keys, per-request params, and the token history the
penalties count over.

- GEN accepts min_p=F penalty_last_n=N penalty_repeat=F penalty_freq=F
  penalty_present=F between max_new and the ids (the server's
  spelling); the engine clamps defensively (min_p to 0..1, a negative
  last_n to 0) and skips what it does not know, as before.
- min_p cuts the top_k survivors to the prefix with p >= min_p * p_max
  - in logits, sel_logit >= sel_logit[0] + logf(min_p) - before top_p,
  so the two cuts compose; 0 disables, and the head always survives,
  so the kept count never reaches zero.
- the penalties need the token history: the serve loop uploads the
  last penalty_last_n tokens - the consumed tail plus the fed-back
  head, which joins consumed_seq only after the window commits - into
  one device row before every window.  A request without penalties
  hands the sampler a null row and takes the byte-for-byte neutral
  path (no upload, nothing handed over).

Verified: sampler_parity grows a full-chain host reference (the Philox
draw transcribed host-side) and fixtures for the sampled chain with
penalties and for min_p at 0/0.5/0.9 - the kernel matches the
reference on all of them, and each fixture first asserts it can SEE
the feature before asserting the kernel matches.  On the IQ3_XXS
artifact, same seed: a request with neutral penalty keys is
token-identical to one without them; a six-copy prompt that loops
24/24 on one token clean produces 24 distinct tokens with repeat 1.5
+ present 0.5; min_p 0.9 changes the pick.

perf(sm75): 超连接投影改走 fp16 张量核（Turing 上 4×，prefill +14%）

背景：sm_75 没有 bf16 张量核，cuBLAS 的 bf16 GEMM 在 Turing 上退回 FFMA。
引擎自带的 STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING 实测该段（hc read，超连接低秩投影
10240->320->10240 x 2 half x 48 层）占 28K prompt GPU 时间的 19.5%（3610 ms）。

改法（arena 保持 bf16，解码路径零改动）：
- 新增 STRATA_TC_SM75 门控（默认 auto：cc==7.5 启用，可置 0 退回旧路径）；
- 新增 bf16_to_f16 批量转换核：16bit->16bit、逐值无损（加载期已验范围）；
- norm/silu 三个 kernel 增加可选 fp16 镜像输出（默认 nullptr，原调用点行为不变）；
- 超连接三处投影在 Turing 上把权重逐矩阵转换到 6.55MB 暂存区后走 Gemm::f16。
  （不采用"arena 常驻 fp16 副本"：需 1.9GB 显存且解码路径按 bf16 读同一份权重。）

实测（2x2080Ti 22GB，Coder IQ1_M，K=26，256 greedy）：
- hc read 3610ms(19.5%) -> 910ms(5.6%)，3.97x
- prefill 1K 603->705 (+17%)、4K 1018->1154 (+13%)、28K 1372->1565 (+14%)
- 每窗口 GPU 时间 37.2->36.1 ms（解码算力不回退）
- 质量：官方 needle 32K 三个深度 3/3 命中；输出与基线同质

踩坑记录：首次实现漏了 gr_write_norm_rs（第三个写 xn16 的 kernel），
该路径下 fp16 镜像是陈旧值 -> needle 0/3、回答幻觉；补齐后 3/3。

perf(sm75): indexer block scores 每 warp 处理 8 个 block（数值不变）

qsa select 在 2,048-token chunk 上占 8.6-9.5%（70 ms/chunk）。该 kernel 每个
warp 只算一个 block（4 head x 128 dim 点积 = 每 lane 32 次乘加），却要做 20 次
shuffle 归约 —— 时间几乎全花在归约上。

改法：q 每个 head 只加载一次，warp 内循环 8 个 block。**每个 block 的算术与
原 kernel 逐值相同**（同样的 partial、同样的 5 级 xor 归约树、同样的顺序），
所以不可能改变任何分数；变的只是消除了重复加载并给了 warp 8 倍的工作量来
隐藏 key 的访存延迟。门控 STRATA_TC_SM75，原 kernel 保留。

实测：qsa select 70 -> ~45 ms/chunk；4K 1,477 -> 1,492、28K 2,110 -> 2,141；
needle 32K 3/3。

Turing 没有 cp.async，所以移植版里 cp_async16 是同步的 load+store：第二级
kv 缓冲不提供任何重叠，却让 smem 从 28.4KB 涨到 44.3KB（Turing 每 SM 64KB，
于是每 SM 只能放 1 个 block）。

1. sm_75 用单级缓冲（PA_STAGES=1）：拷贝移到 compute 之后（单级下必须如此），

2. 把拷贝拆成"加载到寄存器"和"写入 stage"两半：load 在 compute 之前发起、

背景：`Gemm::native` 每次乘法前把原生量化块反量化到 scratch，prompt 路径的稠密投影
（Q5_K/Q6_K/IQ4_XS，形状 6144x2560 / 10240x2560 / 2560x640 等）都走它。原 kernel
每个线程算一个 32 元素组、用 put() **逐元素 2 字节写**：同一条 store 指令跨 lane 相距
64 字节 → 每条指令 32 个 2 字节事务。实测该 kernel 只跑到行带宽的约 18%。

- `dequant_kernel` 增加模板参数 VEC：sm_75 用 `__align__(16) T buf[32]` + 4 次 uint4
  写（float 形式 8 次），其余架构保持原 kernel；
- 内层循环补 `#pragma unroll`，让缓冲留在寄存器而不是本地内存；
- 选择由 `tc_sm75_enabled(major, minor)` 决定 —— **只对 cc 7.5 生效**。

- prefill 4K 1,504-1,542 → **1,594 / 1,615**（+5%）
- prefill 28K 2,188-2,189 → **2,311 / 2,284**（+5.5%）
- decode 73.0-73.5 / 50.3-51.2（不变）；needle 32K 3/3

nsys：`copy16_kernel` 8,651 次、每次 8.7 µs、2.15 MB → 约 247 GB/s（峰值 531）。
逐专家的 16 个 256 线程 block 填不满卡；本改动在组边界（MMQ_GROUP 个专家）发一次

**数值逐字节不变**：同样的字节、同样的目标槽位，只改拷贝的调度；专家 blob 的存活由
原来的 per-expert 事件改为组边界统一记录（staging 槽位在事件记录前不会被复用）。

实测（2×2080 Ti）：4K 1,582/1,617（与 1,594/1,615 持平）、28K **2,321/2,322**

仅对 cc 7.5 生效（`m.grp_src_dev` 只在 tc_sm75() 时分配，否则走原 per-expert 路径）。

fix(sm75): 把 prompt 期新增缓冲计入显存预算（消除"靠公式余量"的隐患）

本树为 sm_75 加的 fp16 镜像与权重暂存（xn16h = chunk*hc*n_embd*2 = 42 MB @2048、lo16h 1.3 MB、
hc_w16 6.55 MB，合计约 50 MB）此前只是**靠经验公式的余量**装下的：prompt 缓冲各自 cudaMalloc（无
borrow）时，专家缓存由 `prefill_mib = 160 + chunk*680/1024`（=1,520 MiB @2048）决定 —— 公式早于
这些缓冲存在。实测边界：余量约能容纳 50 MB，再加 13 MB 的缓冲即触发
`prefill copy_i32: an illegal memory access`。

改法：`sm75_prompt_extra_bytes()` 按 `Prefill::init` 的真实尺寸算出这些字节，并在三处 reserve 计算
（层切分 planner 的 `stage_room`、单卡自动缓存、层切分显式缓存）里补回；**仅对 cc 7.5 生效**
（`tc_sm75_enabled`），其他 SM 型号的预算公式逐字不变。

rebase 到 0.1.30 后的接线（同一改动的第二次落地）：0.1.30 给层切分也开了 prompt 借用（`pf_borrow`；
此前层切分强制 `no_prefill_borrow`），于是 `prefill_mib`/`split_pf_mib` 只在**非借用**时为非零，
借用路径改由 `Prefill::bytes_needed` 精确计价（每次 loan 都按它定尺寸）。故这三处补回改为**跟随同一
个谓词**（`prefill_mib > 0` / `split_pf_mib > 0` 才加），避免借用路径重复计账；`bytes_needed` 一侧
已由 de01052 与 `init` 对齐（含这三个缓冲），借用路径不会少算。

详见报告 §6.7。）

bench(sm75): 新增 prompt attention 微基准，并定位其真实瓶颈（KV 重复读）

新增 `bench/micro/qsa_prompt_attn_bench.cu`（复用 `qsa_prompt_attn_parity` 的输入搭建，
只加计时；`-DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON` 时构建，参数 `ctx nq reps`）。

实测（2×2080 Ti，24 heads / hd 256，单次 `qsa_prompt_attn_batch`）：
| ctx | cap | ms | 有效带宽 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 1024 | 2.65 | **406 GB/s** |
| 2048 | 2048 | 7.04 | 305 GB/s |
| 4096 | 2051 | 13.95 | **154 GB/s** |
| 8192 | 2051 | 14.04 | 153 GB/s |

时间随 `nq × cap` **严格线性**（nq 512/1024/2048 → 3.6/7.0/14.0 ms），但有效带宽随 cap
增大而塌陷：**瓶颈是每个 query 各自 gather 自己选中的 cell 造成的 KV 重复读** ——
ctx=1024 时 KV 池 6.3 MB 可进 L2（406 GB/s），ctx≥4096 时池 25 MB 超出 L2，2048 个 query
把同一批 cell 反复从 DRAM 读（2.15 GB/次），故只有 154 GB/s、0.31 TFLOP/s（fp16 峰值的 0.7%）。

结论：该 kernel **既非算力受限也非带宽上限**，而是被 gather 的重复读限住；对 cap 接近 ctx
（4K 档选择近乎稠密）的情形，改走"KV tile 常驻 smem、块内 query 共享"的稠密路径预计可把
DRAM 流量降约 3×（→ 时间约 5 ms/层）。属结构性改造，未在本轮落地，记入报告 §6.7。

diag(prefill): 选择重叠探针支持任意 tile 大小（STRATA_SEL_TILE）

原探针把 tile 固定为 16 个 query，故只能回答"16 query 共享 KV 能省多少"。
本改动把 tile 大小参数化（`STRATA_SEL_TILE`，默认 16，仅影响 `STRATA_SEL_OVERLAP=1`
时的调试输出，不设该 env 时行为逐字不变），于是可以量出**设计点**的读流量比。

实测（4K prompt，引擎真实选择；`并集/总和` 即共享 staging 后的读流量比）：

| 共享 KV 的 query 数 | 1（现状） | 2 | **4** | 8 | 16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 读流量比 | 100.0% | 55.2% | **31.7%** | 18.2% | 9.2% |

即：**4 个 query 共享一次 KV staging 可把读流量降到 31.7%（3.15×）**，而 16 个可降到
9.2%（10.9×）。这为"prompt attention 多 query 共享 KV tile"的重写给出定量设计点：
现 kernel 每 block = 1 query × 12 head（smem `qh/ql[16][QS]` ≈ 16 KB，每 SM 2 block）；
改成 **4 query × 3 head**（head 槽位仍 12 个 ⇒ **smem 不变、占用率不变**）即可拿到 3.15×
的读流量下降 —— 该 kernel 目前正是被这些重复读限在 154 GB/s（见 bench/micro/qsa_prompt_attn_bench.cu）。

bench(sm75): 让 native_mmvq 的多列布局可由开关选择，并实测其在 sm_75 上不更快

`native_mmvq.hpp` 把 ncols > 1 的两种布局写成了「true（默认）= ncols == 1 的布局，
逐列与单列调用 bitwise 相等；false = llama.cpp 的通用多列表，只到浮点舍入相等，
**速度未测**」，而 `g_multi_exact` 默认 true、引擎里没有任何调用点——只有
`mmvq_multi_parity` 会设它。也就是说那条上游布局在本仓**不可达**，注释里的
「未测」永远不会有答案。

本提交在 graph capture 之前把 `STRATA_MMVQ_MULTI_EXACT` 接到
`native_mmvq_set_multi_exact`，让两种布局都能被真实引擎跑到（默认不变，仍是
bitwise 精确的那一种）。

实测（2× RTX 2080 Ti，Q2_0，4K prompt，256 token，交替 A/B，3 rep，判据
W = decode_ms / windows）：

  MULTI_EXACT=1（默认）  W = 26.90 / 27.12 / 27.60 ms，中位 27.11
  MULTI_EXACT=0（上游表） W = 27.72 / 27.76 / 27.84 ms，中位 27.76

3/3 rep 一致地慢 2.4%，分布不重叠。**上游那条通用多列表在 sm_75 上不更快，
默认值是对的**——这条把源码里的「未测」变成了实测结论，也让下一个想动这块的人
不必再猜。

`-DCUDA_ARCH=80;120` 通过，44 个 kernel 目标里 0 个 sm_75 cubin。

decode: batch the verify window's per-token kernels (bit-identical)

Cherry-picked from upstream 1e4515c (PR #109) onto the fork main, with the

prefill: tile the QSA block scorer's key reads across queries (bit-identical)

The indexer's block-scores kernel launched one warp per (query, block) pair and
re-read its 512 B of fp32 pooled key from DRAM for every query, so the whole
indexer's traffic was O(nq * n_bid) and grew quadratically over a prompt's
chunks: ~54 TB of key reads for a 256K prompt, the measured long-context
collapse (the same kernel runs in the verify window, where it is the biggest
context-scaled decode term).

Each warp now holds its key row in registers and scores a tile of 8 queries
against it (QSA_SCORE_QUERY_TILE / QSA_SCORE_KEY_GROUPS), cutting the key
traffic by the tile factor while keeping the exact per-(query, block)
arithmetic of the old kernel - the scores are bit-identical (qsa_parity
--selftest passes unchanged, including the tie-cut selection test).

Measured on the V100, Q2_0, 262144 context (uncached rows, 64 generated
tokens; block-scores microbench: 2.5-3.7x faster at the engine's real
sel_batch=256 x up to 65K blocks):

  prompt 128K: 805.5 -> 968.3 tok/s (+20%)
  prompt 256K: 396.3 -> 470.3 tok/s (+19%)
  decode @128K: 33.6 -> 38.2 tok/s, @256K: 34.7 -> 40.4 tok/s

(these rows also carry the batched verify-window decode change; the decode
gain breaks down as roughly 2/3 the batched windows and 1/3 the tiled
scorer at long context).

prefill: Volta m8n8k4 tensor-core prompt attention (1.6-1.9x on the QSA kernel)

The V100 ran the FP32 decode-style attention for prompts (qsa_prompt_attn_batch
refused cc<8), which was the largest remaining prefill cost.  This commit ports the
tensor-core prompt attention to Volta:

- mma.m8n8k4 (the f16 MMA shape of sm_70) replaces mma.m16n8k16: one k16 window
  becomes four instructions; computations 0 and 1 carry the two 8-row halves of the
  16-row tile, and the C frame per lane becomes 2 heads x 4 cells or dims.  The
  fragment maps were validated bit-exactly against an FP64 reference on the V100
  before the port.

The prompt path always staged each pinned expert through a host->device DMA into a ring and had the compute stream wait on it. On Swift/gfx1201 the engine's own phase timing showed that staging was the bottleneck: wait copy ~30% and the per-expert gather ~21% of the prompt, with the MMQ GEMM only ~8%. The staged path still copies the blob a second time (staging -> group slot).

The short chunk path now reads a pinned expert directly from the arena's device alias (REBAR) inside the gather/dequant, with no staging DMA and no copy stream. Measured: 39-token prefill 2341 -> 1205 ms (16.93 -> 32.36 tok/s), output bit-identical (the expert bytes are unchanged, only how they reach the SMs). Default ON; STRATA_PREFILL_DIRECT=0 restores the staging path. Only the short path (--prefill < 2048); an expert with no device alias still stages.

docs: 45-paper synthesis for the FP4/MoE/KV path, filtered to gfx1031

RESEARCH_NOTES.md. 45 arXiv papers, fetched in full, extracted by three
Poolside agents in parallel, then every cited number re-checked against
source. Verdicts: 21 ADOPT, 8 ADOPT-HYBRID, 7 DEFER, 9 REJECT.

The filter is the target, not the topic. gfx1031 has no FP4/INT4 MMA, no
WMMA-INT, no sparse tensor cores, and ~350 GB/s. That disqualifies every
paper whose contribution is "run FP4 on the FP4 tensor core" on contact,
however good the algorithm - which is most of them. What survives is the
software-only work, and there is more of it than expected.

Findings that change the plan:

  - INT8 activations, not FP4. 2606.12280 runs INT8 W8A8 on an RTX 3090,
    which has no FP8 tensor cores, and lands statistically
    indistinguishable from FP8 (LPIPS 0.243 vs 0.277/0.306). 2510.25602 has
    MXINT8 beating FP at 8 bits on both accuracy and efficiency; 2606.23406
    has int8 beating fp8 post-Hadamard. 2609.33135 shows the converse trap:
    fully-FP4 attention does not convert tensor-core throughput into
    end-to-end speed. So: 4-bit weights, INT8 activations, __dp4a math. Our
    existing plan was right and now has independent support.

  - GDN weights and GDN state are different objects, and conflating them is
    the most damaging possible misreading of this corpus. 2609.04098
    quantizes all 496 linear layers of a hybrid 27B to NVFP4 W4A4 *including*
    the GDN block, and finds the supposedly fragile gates are the LEAST
    sensitive (~11% GEMM error compresses to ~2% output error). 2608.27513
    and 2609.38169 both find uniform INT8/FP4 of the recurrent *state*
    already degrades accuracy, needing ~6-10 bits. Both are right. Keep state
    F32; quantize the weights.

  - 2603.19289 attacks exactly our bottleneck: speculating future experts from
    current internal representations to overlap the transfer, 14% TPOT. Our
    path is disk-to-VRAM behind a hot LRU, so the number will not transfer,
    but the mechanism is the one we want.

  - 2605.20315 and 2609.26333 independently split the phases: prefill wants
    compute-format quantization, decode wants weight compaction. 2609.26333's
    ODP streams its prefiller from SSD for 1.78x TTFT at 8K in llama.cpp -
    the same shape as our disk-streamed prefill.

  - 2603.10031 (MI325X) states the MLA constraint we needed: MLA requires
    block size 1 and cannot use KV offloading, while GQA benefits from both.
    2609.15030 supplies the matching correctness discipline for GLM (strict-
    prefix lookup, per-rank kernel pinning) after a silent off-by-one-token
    resume bug.

  - 2603.08713's OAS/MBS cut the MXFP4-vs-NVFP4 gap from ~10% to under 1% for
    6.2% GEMM overhead, software-only - unusually valuable when we already pay
    the unpack in software anyway.

Errors corrected, which is the reason to keep the provenance section:

  - An agent report gave NVFP4 as 17 B/16 elem (1.0625 B/elem). Real value is
    36 B/64 elem (0.5625 B/elem) - a 47% overstatement that voids any capacity
    or bandwidth estimate built on it. 16 is the scale *sub-block* size, not
    the storage block; ggml-common.h is the source of truth and the layout is
    recorded from code, not from a paper. (2609.24519 independently confirms
    the E2M1 codebook: 2xFP4 = {0,+-1,+-2,+-3,+-4,+-6,+-8,+-12}, all residues
    mod 13.)
  - Two numbers attributed to 2609.14060 (AGENTQ) appear nowhere in it; both
    belong to 2609.36722 (ATTUNER). A plausible number is not a citation.
  - 2605.12327's abstract is truncated mid-sentence in the fetched metadata,
    so its premise is captured and its result is not guessed.
  - Verification method, and why it took two passes: HTML-to-text extraction
    drops exactly the digits that matter, because arXiv wraps them in LaTeX
    spans. Checking abstracts first took us from 30/45 to 43/45 verified.

perf(deepseek2): head-batched MLA MMVQ - decode 12.46 -> 14.57 tok/s

The deepseek2 token path is HOST-ENQUEUE-BOUND, not GPU-bound: a `--no-pool`

1. Quantize the concatenated per-head activations once (`b.act_q8`, sized

   pointer per head. Q8_1 is per-32-block independent, so this is identical.
2. `native_mmvq_heads`: the `n_head` independent matrix-vector products in ONE
   launch - a `blockIdx.z` head offset over UNCHANGED single-matrix kernels.
   Q8_0 (wk_b) and Q6_K (wv_b); any other type falls back to the per-head loop.

fix: harden multi-session lane scheduling after affinity overwrite regression

The first session-affinity hotfix stored only one affinity key per lane. A short unrelated request could therefore reuse a lane after a long turn completed, overwrite that key, and make the long conversation's next turn route to another GPU and pay a full prompt re-prefill.

Replace per-lane single-owner affinity with a bounded session-to-lane LRU map. Keep busy lifetime request/stream-scoped and affinity lifetime session-scoped. Existing sessions wait for their remembered eligible lane instead of spilling. New sessions never enter a busy lane; among idle eligible lanes they prefer an empty live slot, then the smallest live request state, then the least recently used live state, with rotating order as the final fairness tie-breaker. The policy is hardware-agnostic and contains no GPU-index/model/PCIe-width hardcoding.

Add regression coverage for all-busy queueing, long-session affinity surviving intervening short sessions, live-state-aware placement, bounded affinity state, and vision rebinding. This is serving hardening for the current lane-local KV architecture, not a claim that the scheduling heuristic is the final optimal policy.

fix: make multi-lane wait ordering deterministic

The previous session-affinity hardening still had two scheduler edge cases under contention. First, a completed request without a derivable affinity key left live prompt state but could be misclassified as an empty lane because emptiness was inferred from live_affinity_key=None. Second, when a remembered continuation and a new session were both waiting, Condition.notify_all() allowed the new session to win the wake-up race and steal the continuation's cache-rich lane.

Define empty live state by live_request_bytes == 0, add per-lane affinity waiter reservations, and add compatible FIFO tickets for new-session waiters so older compatible requests receive newly released lanes without letting capability-constrained work block unrelated lanes. Expose queue depth and affinity waiter counts under the scheduler lock for race-safe status reporting.

Add regression coverage for unidentified live state, affinity waiter reservation, four queued requests, LRU tie-breaking, and all-busy release behavior. The generic policy remains hardware-agnostic and contains no GPU-index/model/PCIe-width hardcoding.

hip: fast packed-byte intrinsics for RDNA3/RDNA4 (v_perm_b32 + SWAR)

__byte_perm, __vsub4, __vsubss4 and __vcmpne4 were emulated with
per-lane loops.  On gfx1100/gfx1201 HIP's __byte_perm lowers to private-
memory byte-array traffic in the i-quant table lookups, and the packed
byte loops cost the Q3_K/Q6_K dots and the sign expansion several times
the instructions.

- __byte_perm -> v_perm_b32 in one instruction (selector nibbles spread
  to bytes, masked to 0-7).
- __vsub4/__vsubss4/__vcmpne4 -> branchless SWAR (Hacker's Delight 2-18):
  gfx11/gfx12 have no packed 8-bit add/sub/compare in the ISA, so the
  lane isolation is done with the top-bit trick, not with ISA lanes.
- tests/hip/fast_intrinsics_parity: independent host reference over

  plus randomized mixed-lane words - with output guards.  Registered as

Grouped experts: one weight read for all of a group's entries (NVFP4, Q8_0)

An expert of a verify window is routed from ~1.3 of its tokens; the grouped
kernels ran the whole row dot once per entry, reading and unpacking the

activation every operation is the single dot's, in its order, so each
output is bitwise the old one.  UE4M3 scales are built from their bits
instead of two ldexpf calls (same values on all 256 codes).

telemetry.py reads the GPU through NVML, so on an AMD box (no libnvidia-ml)
every GPU series is absent: the Monitor's GPU load, VRAM, temperature, power and
PCIe cards show "-", and hardware_static.gpu_name is null.  Where psutil is not

_AmdSysfs reads the same fields from amdgpu's sysfs: the card is found by
scanning /sys/class/drm/card*/device for DRIVER=amdgpu (the number is not fixed
- a box with another DRM device can have the AMD card at card1), the
temperature is the hwmon sensor labelled "edge" (what NVML calls the GPU
temperature), power comes from power1_average/power1_cap, and the link from
current/max_link_speed plus current_link_width.  Every reading is a small file
read, so a sample cannot block the server, and anything the kernel does not
expose stays None rather than being invented.  amdgpu has no PCIe throughput
counter, so the link is reported and the MB/s series stays empty; the web app
already renders "Gen4 x16" from those fields.

only, never partitions and never loop/zram/dm, which would count a device-mapper
layer twice) and /proc/cpuinfo's (physical id, core id) pairs for the
psutil-less case.
